title: Sampling applications — Ridgeway Components
instructions: You are evaluating sampling applications in the audit of **Ridgeway Components**. Use the data provided; round percentages to one decimal place.

exhibits.title: Test of controls — purchase approval
exhibits.content:
- Population: 18,400 purchase orders
- Tolerable deviation rate: 6%; acceptable risk of overreliance: 5%
- Sample: 100 purchase orders; deviations found: 2
- Statistical table: upper deviation rate for 2 deviations in 100 at 5% risk = **6.2%**

exhibits.title: Substantive test — receivables (MUS)
exhibits.content:
- Book value: **$4,200,000**; sample size: **120**
- Tolerable misstatement: $210,000
- Misstatements found:
  - Customer A: book $14,000, audited $10,500
  - Customer B: book $52,000, audited $49,000
  - Customer C: book $7,000, audited $6,650

parts.prompt: Conclusion on the test of controls

rows.label: Can the auditor rely on the control as planned?
options: Yes — the sample rate is below the tolerable rate
No — the upper deviation rate exceeds the tolerable rate
rows.answer: No — the upper deviation rate exceeds the tolerable rate
rows.explanation: 6.2% > 6%; the decision uses the upper deviation rate, not the 2% sample rate.

parts.prompt: How would each change affect the attribute sample size, other things equal?

rows.label: Tolerable deviation rate lowered from 6% to 4%
rows.explanation: A lower tolerable rate requires a larger sample.

rows.label: Expected deviation rate raised from 1% to 2%
rows.explanation: More expected deviations require a larger sample.

rows.label: Acceptable risk of overreliance raised from 5% to 10%
rows.explanation: Accepting more risk permits a smaller sample.

rows.label: Population grows from 18,400 to 25,000
rows.explanation: Population size has little effect on large populations.
